messages:
maya: Onboarding intake: 'cardinal-13b' — quick perf triage request. Summary: int8 quant smoke gives ~2x throughput vs bf16 but we're seeing a 3x spike in 99p latency during warmup with long context (>8k). Asking for prioritization: batching profile check, full ctx-length sweep to 16k, and a basic quality regression run vs bf16 baseline.

liam: ack. I'll own the ctx-sweep and heatmap. ETA 24h. @zoe can you do a memory/kernels pass?

zoe: yep. please paste the bench command and the model config you used. suspecting fragmentation with the current allocator flags.

maya: bench command I used:```bash
python run_throughput.py --model cardinal-13b --quant int8 --batch 8 --seq 8192 --warmup 20 --steps 200 --accumulate 1
```Output (abridged):```text
throughput: 102.3 tokens/s
p50 token latency: 12.4ms
p95 token latency: 85.1ms
p99 token latency: 420.7ms
warmup phase (first 40 steps) p99: 1200ms
```Note: bf16 baseline p99 steady-state ~140ms.

bench-bot: Auto-bench summary for run 2572468000-1 — model: cardinal-13b int8
metrics: steady_throughput=102.3, steady_p99=420.7, warmup_p99=1200, mem_peak=24.1GB, gpu_util=78%

jordan: two quick ideas: (1) try prewarming KV cache with a short prefix workload to avoid slow cold KV allocations; (2) lower batch to 4 and enable continuous batching (runtime param) to see if warmup spike moves. I'll test (1) now.

maya: gating thresholds proposal: want throughput >= 1.8x bf16 baseline AND steady_p99 <= 1.5x bf16 p99. If warmup_p99 > 2x bf16, fail for now. Thoughts?

anya: add a quality gate: run the 50-prompt eval set comparing logprob and exact-match on generated completions. If any prompt has >3% drop in utility metric, block. We had subtle regressions on hallucination in earlier int8 runs.

zoe: saw kernel logs showing multiple small allocations during past few steps — attaching example:```text
[alloc] 0x7f8a3c... 12MB
[alloc] 0x7f8a4d... 8MB
[free ] 0x7f8a3c... 12MB
[alloc] 0x7f8a5e... 24MB
```This pattern correlates with the p99 spikes. Will try arena=true allocator + contiguous_cache=true.

liam: I'll run ctx sweep with batch=4/8/16 and seq=[512,2048,8192,12288,16384]. Will produce a heatmap and CSV. Target finish by EOD tomorrow.

jordan: prewarm run (quick):```bash
python prewarm.py --model cardinal-13b --prefix-len 512 --reps 10
```Result: warmup_p99 dropped from 1200ms -> 480ms in that quick test, steady p99 unchanged. Suggests cache priming helps but doesn't eliminate later spikes.

maya: good signal. plan: (1) liam ctx-sweep, (2) zoe kernel/allocator config matrix, (3) anya run quality eval, (4) bench-bot scheduled nightly smoke with prewarm enabled. If all green, we consider promoting int8 to canary.

infra-bot: Noted — created infra ticket INF-4829 for dedicated pool sizing during canary. Link: https://redwood.internal/INF-4829

liam: assigning heatmap -> /owns liam. I'll post CSV + heatmap image here when done.

zoe: I'll run config matrix: allocator=[default,arena], contiguous_cache=[false,true], batcher=[continuous,none]; will prioritize runs that minimize warmup_p99.

anya: I'll run eval and post a quick summary table (metric diffs) and flag any prompt regressions.

maya: thanks all. quick ask: if anyone hits a config that fixes warmup p99 but reduces throughput by >10%, call it out — might be a tradeoff we accept for SLO stability.

jordan: +1. Also suggest adding a short A/B in Redwood Console for canary with traffic ramping 1%->5% over 6 hours.

zoe: repro note: set env RUN_NUMA_PIN=1 when testing on multi-socket nodes, it reduced page migrations in earlier runs.

liam: noted. starting sweep now.

maya: if you can, drop any raw CSVs into /mnt/bench/cardinal-int8/2572468000 for triage. I'll write the onboarding checklist once we have heatmap+eval. :thumbsup:
